# powerjp — detailed project description

## Identity

powerjp is an open-data pipeline and static web map about Japan's electric power system. It joins public source data into inspectable, versioned artifacts and renders them on a Mapbox GL JS map. The project is intended for research, data exploration, and reproducible analysis.

Website: https://powerjp.mkhr.co.jp/

## What is shown

### Network and facilities

- Transmission-line geometry and network topology where the published source data provides a usable, source-backed geometry.
- Substations and their available attributes.
- Generation sites and unit-level output layers where coordinates and source matching are available.

### Time-dependent data

- Observed trunk-line power flow at 30-minute resolution.
- Unit output at 30-minute resolution where OCCTO provides it.
- Hourly area-level supply-demand data is used upstream for derived estimates. The source CSVs are not presented as a raw-data mirror.

## Geographic scope

The geographic scope is Japan. The project uses a country-level geographic description instead of a fake single-point coordinate because this is a national network dataset, not a business at one address.

## Method

1. Source data is ingested into a local, date-stamped raw-data area.
2. Identifiers, coordinates, and time windows are aligned in deterministic processing steps.
3. Static artifacts are written as GeoJSON or JSON.
4. Artifacts are published with a manifest; content-hashed objects are used for atomic CDN updates.
5. The web application reads the manifest and renders only the layers selected by the user.

## What the project does not claim

- It is not an operational dispatch, protection, or grid-control tool.
- Observed flow is not the same as a newly calculated AC power-flow solution.
- Ten-area demand data cannot support building-level demand estimates.
- A missing line geometry does not prove that a physical line does not exist.
- Source-specific licences are not replaced by the MIT licence of the code.

## Sources

- All-Japan-Grid: network and facility topology derived from a community project built on OpenStreetMap.
- OpenStreetMap: upstream geospatial data for the topology-derived artifacts.
- OCCTO: public observed power-flow and unit-output data, modified and aligned by the project.
- MLIT National Land Numerical Information: public facility-coordinate data.
- Global Energy Monitor: generation-facility attributes and coordinates.

The application exposes attribution links and notes. See the published manifest and attribution view before using an artifact downstream.

## Output formats

- GeoJSON for network and facility layers.
- JSON for common time stamps and manifest metadata.
- Static files distributed through Cloudflare R2 or an R2-compatible CDN.

## Licence

The code is MIT licensed. Published artifacts are not automatically covered by that licence. Artifacts derived from All-Japan-Grid/OpenStreetMap carry ODbL obligations, and other inputs may have additional conditions. Consult the source terms and attribution shown by the application.
